- Signs with "Developer ID Application" (hardened runtime, timestamp) when that identity is in the Keychain, else ad hoc; always without the app's entitlements (no macOS provisioning profile exists for the Mac bundle id), except the microphone entitlement in `apps/ios/Resources/MacHardenedRuntime.entitlements`, which needs no profile.
- Writes the binary's SHA-256 to `build/native-sha256.txt`. Not notarized.

The macOS destination's bundle id differs from iOS (`PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER[sdk=macosx*]` in `Project.swift`). A post-build phase copies the plugin (`index.ts`, `setup-entry.ts`, `openclaw.plugin.json`, `package.json`, `README.md`, `src`) into `Contents/Resources/openclaw-channel` on macOS.

sections.heading: Mac: beta and stable releases
sections.text:
`scripts/release_mac.sh` builds into `dist/`:

1. Release build with the Developer ID identity, no entitlements; re-signs Sparkle's nested helpers, the framework and the app; checks the bundle id and that the bundled plugin is present.
2. `Yorozu.dmg`: signed, notarized with the notarytool keychain profile (`NOTARY_PROFILE`, default `yorozu-notary`; up to three tries), stapled.
3. `appcast.xml` from Sparkle's `generate_appcast` (EdDSA-signed; `SPARKLE_ED_KEY_FILE` or the login Keychain), download URLs pointing at the release tag.
4. `candidate.json` (tag, version, `CFBundleVersion`, source commit).

Modes:

- No flag: build only. Visible build is `BUILD`, else the build of the current beta release of this version (from its `candidate.json`) plus one, or 1. It also goes past the highest `v<version>-beta.<n>` tag left from before the single beta, so Sparkle still sees the build rise.
- `--publish`: refuses a dirty tree, deletes the current beta release and its `v<version>-beta` tag (the `release tags` ruleset makes `v*` tags immutable but leaves `*-beta` alone; an older `v<version>-beta.<n>` tag stays, and only its release goes), then creates the prerelease `v<version>-beta` with the three assets and notes from `scripts/release_notes.sh` (feat, fix and perf Conventional Commits since the last stable tag, dependency bumps left out). A version has one beta release, which each build replaces, and there is one beta at a time; when a `feat` lands, the next beta moves to the new minor version.
- `--promote <build> <source sha> <sha256:digest>`: if `v<version>` does not exist yet and the current beta `v<version>-beta` (or an older `v<version>-beta.<n>`) is still exactly the release the release PR named, downloads its assets, points the appcast at the stable release, republishes them as `v<version>`, marked latest, with generated notes, then deletes the beta release and, for `v<version>-beta`, its tag (the beta feed falls back to the stable release until the next beta). Does nothing if `v<version>` exists. Before publishing anything it checks that `candidate.json`'s build is that build's `CFBundleVersion`, its tag is the beta's and its `source_sha` is the named commit; that the release's target commit and the commit the tag points at are the named commit (a moved tag fails); and that `Yorozu.dmg`'s digest, as GitHub reports it and as downloaded, is the named digest. Every mismatch is reported as an error, and it exits 1 without publishing or deleting anything; a missing or malformed argument exits 64.

Stable releases work like release-please. After each beta, `scripts/release_pr.sh` resets the branch `release` to the beta's commit, commits `CHANGELOG.md` with the version's notes through the contents API (so GitHub signs it, as the `main` ruleset requires), opens or updates the PR `chore: release <version>`, whose body ends with `Release-Build: <build>`, `Release-Commit: <source sha>` and `Release-Digest: sha256:<DMG digest>`, and approves the PR's `checks.yml` run, which waits for approval because a bot opened the PR (with only `CHANGELOG.md` changed, both required checks skip, which counts as passing; if the Actions token may not approve, approve it on the PR by hand). Check that beta, then merge the PR: `promote.yml` promotes the named build. A newer beta updates the PR to name it, and `--promote` refuses a beta that is not the named build, commit and DMG; then nothing is promoted, and the next beta opens a new release PR. Merging changes only `CHANGELOG.md`, so it starts no new beta; the next push does.

Feeds and downloads (`apps/web/worker.mjs`, `apps/web/public/_redirects`):

- `yorozu.yumi.to/appcast.xml` and `/mac`: the latest stable release's appcast and DMG.
- `yorozu.yumi.to/beta` and `/beta/appcast.xml`: the newest release, prereleases included.

Release notes come from `scripts/release_notes.sh [<commit>]`: the pull requests merged into `main` since the last stable tag (never a `-beta` tag), each with its number, grouped by the feat, fix and perf Conventional Commits types of their titles, with dependency bumps and other types left out. A PR is a merge `Merge pull request #N …` on `main`'s first-parent line (titled by the merge's body) or a squashed commit ending `(#N)`; a commit pushed straight to `main` counts by its subject. `<` and `>` are escaped for Markdown. Every `--publish` writes them into the beta's body again, so it always lists everything since the last stable release; the release PR, `CHANGELOG.md` and the stable release use the same notes, and `--what-to-test <locale> <version> <build>` gives a TestFlight build's What to Test in one locale ([TestFlight](#ios-and-ipados-testflight)). These notes stay in English: the release body, the release PR and `CHANGELOG.md` are read on GitHub, which has no per-language text.

The Mac app links Sparkle (macOS only, `MacUpdates.swift`): stable feed from `SUFeedURL`, automatic checks and installs every hour; Settings › About has the Sparkle switches, Check Now and the last check; its Update to: Beta Versions switches to the beta feed (`feedURLString(for:)`).

sections.heading: iOS and iPadOS: TestFlight
sections.text:
`scripts/upload_ios.sh --confirm` archives and uploads. Each upload uses up its build number.

- Without `--confirm` it exits 64. Needs `ASC_KEY_ID`, `ASC_ISSUER_ID` and the `.p8` key (`ASC_KEY_PATH`, else `~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_<id>.p8`).
- External TestFlight is off. The repository variable `YOROZU_EXTERNAL_TESTFLIGHT` is unset, and `release-ios.yml` passes it to the upload step. Nothing in CI gives a build to an external TestFlight group or submits it to Beta App Review; a step that ever does must run `scripts/external_testflight.sh` first and stop unless it exits 0, which it does only when the variable is exactly `true` (unset, empty, `false` or `TRUE` exit 1). `scripts/upload_ios.sh` prints the switch's state before it archives. The `release-guards` job in `checks.yml` runs `scripts/external_testflight.sh --audit`, which fails a pull request whose workflows or scripts name an App Store Connect group or Beta App Review call (`betaGroups`, `betaAppReviewSubmissions`, …) without running the switch.
- Visible build: the highest build App Store Connect has for this version, plus one; `BUILD=<n>` skips the lookup. A build reaches that list minutes after its upload (about 15 for 0.10.0 build 6), so after uploading the script waits up to `LIST_WAIT` seconds (default 3600) until App Store Connect lists it, and fails if it never does; `release-ios.yml` runs one upload at a time (concurrency group `release-ios`), so the next merge's upload starts only after the previous build is listed and cannot reuse its number. Either way `build-number.sh` rejects a build past 999 (exit 65): promote, so the next build starts a new version.
- Archives `generic/platform=iOS` only (app plus notification service, share, widgets and asset downloader extensions) with automatic signing and `-allowProvisioningUpdates`. The Mac destination is never uploaded.
- `apps/ios/ExportOptions.plist` (`destination` = `upload`) makes the export step the upload. TestFlight gives processed builds to the internal group.
- After the upload it sets the build's What to Test in every language the app ships in: one folder per App Store Connect locale in `apps/ios/metadata/testflight` (`en-US`, `ja`, `zh-Hans`, `zh-Hant`, `ko`, `es-ES`, `fr-FR`, `de-DE`, `pt-BR`), each giving `scripts/release_notes.sh --what-to-test` its intro (`Yorozu <version> (<build>), beta.` in English), a note, the section headings and the closing line. The PRs are the Mac beta's, with their titles as written: CI has no translation. Each locale's text stays within App Store Connect's 4,000 bytes (past that the list ends with `… and N more`, in that language). A locale the build lacks is created; one it has is set only while empty or still holding this script's text for this build, so What to Test written by hand stays, and locales without a folder are left alone. What to Test belongs to the build, so only the groups that get the build see it: the internal group. The script adds the build to no group and submits nothing to Beta App Review. If App Store Connect refuses the text, the job fails after the upload with an error saying so; set it in App Store Connect by hand.
- The beta app description testers see, per locale, comes from `apps/ios/metadata/testflight/<locale>/description.txt` through `scripts/testflight_metadata.sh`, run by hand and never in CI: it belongs to the app, so external testers see it too. Without `--apply` it only reads App Store Connect and prints what it would change. It creates missing locales and fills empty fields; the feedback email and the marketing and privacy policy URLs are copied from `en-US`, so they live in App Store Connect alone. A description that differs from its file is kept and reported. Running it twice changes nothing the second time.
- The App Store listing per locale (name, subtitle, keywords, promotional text, description, What's New) comes from `apps/ios/metadata/app_store/<locale>/` through `scripts/app_store_metadata.sh`, run by hand and never in CI. It only edits the iOS version already being prepared in App Store Connect and never creates or submits one; `scripts/app_store_submit.sh` does that. Without `--apply` it only reads and prints its plan. Like the beta description, it creates missing locales, fills empty fields, copies the URLs from `en-US`, and keeps and reports text that differs from its file. `--check` checks the files against App Store Connect's limits offline, and Checks runs it on every PR.
- Screenshots and the product page art per locale come from `apps/ios/metadata/app_store/<locale>/screenshots/<device>/` and `<locale>/creative/` through `scripts/app_store_media.sh [--version <x.y.z>] [--carry-en-us] [--apply]`, run by hand and never in CI. It only edits an iOS version App Store Connect still lets you edit (exit 65 otherwise). Without `--apply` it only reads App Store Connect and prints its plan; with it, it runs that plan first and stops if anything blocks. It checks every file against the image specs App Store Connect publishes (pixel size, alpha, file type and size, `appAssetLibraryRefData`) and against the per-group limits (10 screenshots, 1 header, 1 search image), uploads each file to the app's asset library once (the reference name carries its checksum), places it in that locale and orders the group: the repo's files first, then those already there. A locale with screenshots of its own stops showing en-US's, and the plan says so; `--carry-en-us` places en-US's others after its own. Exit codes: 64 bad arguments, 65 blocked, 70 App Store Connect refused a write, 1 no key.
- App Store submission: `scripts/app_store_submit.sh <version> <build> [--release-type MANUAL|AFTER_APPROVAL] [--create] [--attach] [--submit]`, run by hand and never in CI (review notes: `apps/ios/APP-REVIEW-NOTES.md`). Without a flag it only reads App Store Connect and prints its plan, exiting 65 with the reason if anything would stop it. `--create` creates the iOS version if it is missing, else reuses it, and sets its release type (default: that of the newest version on sale). `--attach` attaches the build, only if it is `VALID`, not expired and uploaded for that version. `--submit` reuses an open review submission or creates one, adds the version once, and submits it. It reports the content rights declaration and the build's export compliance against `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` in `apps/ios/Project.swift`, and writes nothing while any of these block. Every step reads App Store Connect again first, so running it twice changes nothing the second time. Exit codes: 64 bad arguments, 65 blocked, 70 App Store Connect refused a write. For example, `scripts/app_store_submit.sh 0.10.0 1000010`, then the same with `--create --attach`, and `--submit` once the owner approves the submission.

sections.heading: Background modes and entitlements
sections.text:
The iOS app declares two `UIBackgroundModes` in `apps/ios/Project.swift`, each explained to App Review in `apps/ios/APP-REVIEW-NOTES.md`:

- `remote-notification`: a push wakes the app to fetch the reply.
- `audio`: live dictation continues while the user switches apps, until they stop it. Voice input records with the `.record` audio session category; the system's microphone indicator stays on the whole time, and the Live Activity's recording row has Stop and Cancel. Nothing plays and nothing records unless the owner started voice input.

`BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers` lists `to.yumi.yorozu.ios.voice-transcribe.*`, the iOS 26 continued-processing task that finishes a GPU voice engine's transcription after the owner leaves the app, and the app target has the `com.apple.developer.background-tasks.continued-processing.gpu` entitlement so that task may keep the GPU. Signing needs that capability on the App ID, which automatic signing adds to the profile.

sections.heading: Voice model asset packs
sections.text:
On iPhone and iPad each downloaded voice model is an Apple-hosted, on-demand asset pack, uploaded once and updated independently of app builds. The pack IDs and files are in `packages/YorozuVoice/Sources/VoiceText/VoiceCatalog.swift`:

| Pack ID | Model | Files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VoiceModel` | LFM3-Audio-2B | 1,437,488,096 bytes at the pack's root (uploaded; leave it as it is) |
| `VoiceWhisperTurbo` | Whisper Large v3 Turbo (Core ML) | 739,798,664 bytes in `whisper-large-v3-turbo/`, plus its `LICENSE.txt` |
| `VoiceWhisperSmall` | Whisper Small (Core ML) | 489,357,480 bytes in `whisper-small/`, plus its `LICENSE.txt` |
| `VoiceNemotron` | Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming 0.6B (Core ML) | 615,434,988 bytes in `nemotron-3.5-asr/`, plus its `LICENSE.txt` (OpenMDW-1.1 requires the license with the weights) |

`scripts/voice_asset_pack.sh <pack ID> <dir>` downloads the pinned files, checks their sizes and SHA-256 and writes `<dir>/<pack ID>/<pack ID>.aar`. Upload it with `altool` and the same App Store Connect API key the scripts use (`ASC_KEY_ID`, `ASC_ISSUER_ID`), without an Apple ID login, then submit it for review in App Store Connect with a build:

```sh
xcrun altool --upload-asset-pack <dir>/<pack ID>/<pack ID>.aar --apple-id <app Apple ID> \
    --api-key "$ASC_KEY_ID" --api-issuer "$ASC_ISSUER_ID" --p8-file-path "$ASC_KEY_PATH" --wait
```

`--apple-id` is the app's numeric Apple ID from App Store Connect, not a login. Without `--p8-file-path`, `altool` looks for `AuthKey_<ASC_KEY_ID>.p8` in `./private_keys`, `~/private_keys`, `~/.private_keys`, `~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys` or `$API_PRIVATE_KEYS_DIR`. `--wait` waits until App Store Connect has processed the pack; `xcrun altool --list-asset-pack-versions --apple-id <app Apple ID> --asset-pack-identifier <pack ID>` (with the same key flags) lists what it has. Transporter's command-line tool, `iTMSTransporter`, refuses to run unless the Transporter app is installed, so use `altool`. A new model revision needs the script's file list, `VoiceCatalog.swift` and the pack updated together; `swift test --package-path packages/YorozuVoice` fails while the script and the catalogue differ.

Until App Store Connect has processed a version of a pack, the system knows no pack with that ID (`ManagedBackgroundAssetsError.assetPackNotFound`): Settings › Voice Input › Model shows that model as Not available yet, and Settings › Voice Input says the model isn’t available for this version yet, with Try Again; the underlying error goes to the log that Copy Diagnostics includes. Internal TestFlight uses the latest processed version on its own; external TestFlight needs that version approved in TestFlight App Review, and the App Store needs it approved in a review submission, alone or with an app version. Check what App Store Connect has with `GET /v1/apps/{id}/backgroundAssets`. Apple Speech needs no pack: the system installs its languages.

sections.heading: Compile checks
sections.text:
The commands `checks.yml` runs, without signing, uploading or touching `/Applications` (CI adds `-quiet`):

```sh
mise install                                   # Tuist
tuist generate --no-open --path apps/ios
# iPhone and iPad, with both extensions
env -u SDKROOT xcodebuild build -workspace apps/ios/Yorozu.xcworkspace -scheme YorozuIOS \
    -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -derivedDataPath .build/xcode-ios \
    -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath .build/xcode-packages -skipPackagePluginValidation \
    CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO
# Mac
env -u SDKROOT xcodebuild build -workspace apps/ios/Yorozu.xcworkspace -scheme YorozuIOS \
    -destination 'platform=macOS' -derivedDataPath .build/xcode-mac \
    -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath .build/xcode-packages -skipPackagePluginValidation \
    CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO
```

Not in CI:

```sh
swift build --package-path packages/YorozuWire   # the wire package alone
pnpm --filter @yorozu/web test                   # the website (deploy-web.yml runs it before deploying)
```

The plugin typechecks per [its README](../plugins/openclaw-yorozu/README.md#typecheck).

- **Simulator**: generate with `TUIST_VOICE_INPUT=0 tuist generate --no-open --path apps/ios` (llama.cpp's xcframework has no simulator slice, so this leaves LFM3-Audio-2B out of voice input), then build for `platform=iOS Simulator,id=<udid>` with `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=` instead of `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`; an unsigned simulator build has no Keychain entitlement, so saving a pairing fails. Install and launch with `xcrun simctl install <udid> <app>` and `xcrun simctl launch <udid> <iOS bundle id>`.
- **Mac dev build**: the Mac compile check builds Debug at `.build/xcode-mac/Build/Products/Debug/YorozuIOS.app` under the installed app's bundle id. To run one, add `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER=<an id of its own>` so it never passes for `/Applications/Yorozu.app`. It is ad hoc signed (runs only on the Mac that built it; Keychain prompts after each rebuild), and its Keychain items still use the iOS bundle id as service, so pairing or unpairing in it can replace or delete the installed app's pairing.

sections.heading: Website and relay
sections.text:
- `apps/web`: Astro site served by a Cloudflare Worker (`worker.mjs`, `wrangler.jsonc`) at yorozu.yumi.to. `pnpm --filter @yorozu/web dev|build|test`; `pnpm --filter @yorozu/web run deploy` deploys by hand. Its `/pair` page and `.well-known/apple-app-site-association` open the app from the pairing QR's web link (`applinks:yorozu.yumi.to`), so those paths must stay.
- `apps/relay`: Cloudflare Worker with Durable Objects (`wrangler.toml`) at relay.yumi.to. `pnpm --filter @yorozu/relay test` runs its typecheck and tests.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
# Setup

How to put Yorozu on an OpenClaw Gateway, pair a device and chat, plus what building the client needs. Run the OpenClaw commands below on the computer that runs the Gateway, from the repository root of the main checkout. The parts are described in [architecture.md](architecture.md), and the plugin's behaviour in [its README](../plugins/openclaw-yorozu/README.md).

## Tools

| Need | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| OpenClaw | 2026.9.8 or later (`peerDependencies` in `plugins/openclaw-yorozu/package.json`) | The `openclaw` CLI on `PATH` and a running Gateway. The Gateway loads the plugin's TypeScript from source; there is no build step. |
| Xcode | 27 (CI uses 27.1) | Builds the client (`apps/ios`) and `packages/YorozuWire`. |
| Tuist | pinned in `mise.toml` | Install with `mise install`. The generated Xcode project and workspace are gitignored. |
| Upload tools | system | `scripts/upload_ios.sh` also uses `openssl`, `curl`, `jq`, `awk` and `xxd`. |

## 1. Install the plugin

```sh
openclaw plugins install --link plugins/openclaw-yorozu --force --accept-capabilities
openclaw gateway restart
openclaw channels status
```

- `--link` loads the plugin from this directory, and code changes load on the next Gateway restart. Link from a checkout that stays, not from a worktree that will be removed.
- `--force` accepts a source that is not on ClawHub. `--accept-capabilities` gives the capability consent that the install otherwise stops to ask for.
- No `channels.yorozu` entry is needed, because every key has a default ([Config](#2-config)).
- On first start the plugin makes its host keys. The Gateway log shows `yorozu started (agent <agent>, room <room id>)`, then `yorozu: registered at relay, room <room id>`, and `openclaw channels status` shows the Yorozu channel connected.
- The Mac app also carries a copy of the plugin at `Yorozu.app/Contents/Resources/openclaw-channel`. A Gateway linked there runs the plugin version of the installed app.

The `openclaw yorozu` commands reach the running plugin through Gateway methods, so the Gateway must be running with the channel connected. They accept the usual Gateway client options (`--url`, `--port`, `--token`, `--password`, `--timeout`).

To try the plugin without touching a Gateway in use, run it in an isolated OpenClaw profile ([plugin README](../plugins/openclaw-yorozu/README.md#trying-it-without-the-main-gateway)).

## 2. Config

Every key under `channels.yorozu` is optional:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `channels.yorozu.enabled` | `true` | `false` stops the channel |
| `channels.yorozu.agent` | `main` | The agent that answers every Yorozu conversation, and whose cron jobs the Automations tab lists |
| `channels.yorozu.relayUrl` | `wss://relay.yumi.to` | The relay that the plugin and the apps meet on. It goes into the pairing link. |
| `channels.yorozu.mediaMaxMb` | `agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb`, else 128 | Attachment size limit, both ways |
| `channels.yorozu.textChunkLimit` | 4000 | Longest reply chunk, in characters |

```sh
openclaw config set channels.yorozu.agent <agent id>
```

The plugin declares `channels.yorozu` as its reload prefix, so OpenClaw restarts the channel when that config changes. Changing `relayUrl` moves the host to another relay, so every device has to pair again.

### Owner-only tools

OpenClaw treats a Yorozu turn as a non-owner sender, so its owner-only agent tools are denied. That includes `automations`, which the Automations tab's "Edit in Chat" needs. To give Yorozu turns owner authority, add `yorozu:owner` to `commands.ownerAllowFrom` and keep the entries already there:

```sh
openclaw config get commands.ownerAllowFrom
openclaw config set commands.ownerAllowFrom '[<existing entries>, "yorozu:owner"]' --strict-json
```

This gives every paired device the owner's authority over the agent.

### OpenClaw updates

Yorozu does not update OpenClaw. OpenClaw's own auto-update does it: when the Gateway is idle, it drains running turns, updates, restarts and checks the result, and rolls back if that fails. Meanwhile the apps show the Gateway as offline. Auto-update needs both of these:

- `update.auto.enabled` set to `true` (it is off by default), with `update.checkOnStart` not `false` and `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` not set:

  ```sh
  openclaw config set update.auto.enabled true
  ```

- The Gateway running as a managed service (launchd, systemd or a Scheduled Task). A Gateway started in a terminal only logs that an update is available:

  ```sh
  openclaw gateway install
  ```

If either is missing, the plugin posts a notice into the most recent conversation after the Gateway starts. It posts it again only when what is missing changes. After an update, it posts `Updated OpenClaw <old> → <new>` there once ([plugin README](../plugins/openclaw-yorozu/README.md#gateway-notices-srcupdatests)). OpenClaw's own guide: `docs/install/updating/automatic-updates.md` in the OpenClaw source.

### Models

Yorozu has no model settings of its own; it uses the configured agent's models. Titles come from OpenClaw's title generator, which uses the agent's utility model first and then its primary model. Attachments reach the model as media, so pictures need a model that accepts image input.

## 3. Install a client

- **iPhone, iPad**: the Yorozu app from TestFlight or the App Store ([release.md](release.md#ios-and-ipados-testflight)).
- **Mac**: `scripts/build_native.sh` builds the client into `/Applications/Yorozu.app` ([release.md](release.md#mac-local-build)).

The app and the plugin speak the same wire; old clients keep working ([contract](ios-relay-contract.md#frames)).

## 4. Pair a device

```sh
openclaw yorozu pair
```

The command prints a QR code, a `yorozu://pair?…` link, the host fingerprint and the expiry time. The code works for one device, within 10 minutes, and only until the next Gateway restart.

1. In the app, on "Pair with your host", do one of these:
   - On iPhone or iPad, tap Scan QR Code and scan the code.
   - On any device, paste the link (or the https link the QR encodes) with Paste, or type it into "Pairing link" and tap Pair.
2. The app asks "Pair with this host?" and shows the host key. Pair only if it matches the fingerprint the command printed.
3. Pairing is done when the conversation list appears and `openclaw yorozu devices` lists the device by its model name. The app then asks to allow notifications.

**From a paired device:** Settings › Add a Device… makes a fresh pairing code on the host and shows it as a QR code and a link.

**A new Mac from a paired iPhone or iPad:** the Mac's pairing screen shows a code, which changes every 10 minutes.

1. On the iPhone or iPad, open Settings › Add a Device › Scan a Mac's Code (or point the Camera at the code) and tap Add.
2. On the Mac, check that the host key matches and click Pair.

Pair each device separately; all of them see the same conversations. At most 16 devices can be paired: a 17th replaces the oldest.

### Try demo data without a host

On the pairing screen, enter `YOROZU-DEMO` in **Pairing link** and tap **Pair**, or scan a QR code containing that text. Surrounding whitespace is ignored, and the code is case-sensitive. Demo mode shows sample conversations and automations and gives scripted replies; no host is involved. Settings › **Exit Demo** leaves it, and the existing pairing is kept.

For development, launch with `--demo` to start in demo mode directly. On the Mac, use a dev build with its own bundle id ([release.md](release.md#compile-checks)):

```sh
open -n .build/xcode-mac/Build/Products/Debug/YorozuIOS.app --args --demo
```

On an iOS Simulator with the app installed, run `xcrun simctl launch <udid> to.yumi.yorozu.ios --demo`.

## Devices

```sh
openclaw yorozu devices               # id, name, paired at
openclaw yorozu devices remove <id>   # the id, or a unique start of it
```

`remove` takes the device off the allowlist and tells the relay to forget it and close its sockets. The app then shows "Removed from the host". In the app, Settings lists the paired devices, can turn push on or off for each, and can remove other devices. Settings › Unpair This Device removes this device on the host and deletes its keys and cache.

## Self-hosted relay

The plugin and the apps use the public relay `wss://relay.yumi.to` unless `channels.yorozu.relayUrl` says otherwise. To run your own, use either form of `apps/relay` ([its README](../apps/relay/README.md)):

- **Cloudflare Worker**: in `apps/relay/wrangler.toml`, replace the `relay.yumi.to` route with a domain in your own Cloudflare account, then run `pnpm --filter @yorozu/relay run deploy`.
- **Docker** (Node, keeps everything in memory):

  ```sh
  docker build -f apps/relay/Dockerfile -t yorozu-relay .
  docker run -d --restart unless-stopped -p 8787:8787 yorozu-relay
  ```

  Put it behind a TLS proxy. The apps accept only `wss://`, except `ws://` to `localhost`.

Then point the plugin at it and pair every device again, because the pairing link carries the relay:

```sh
openclaw config set channels.yorozu.relayUrl wss://relay.example.com
openclaw yorozu pair
```

What a self-hosted relay doesn't do:

- **Push:** it can't send push. APNs pushes need the app developer's key, so there are no notifications while the app is closed. The Mac never gets push anyway.
- **Mac pairing codes:** a new Mac's pairing code still goes through the public relay's one-time mailbox. Only the invite link passes there; conversations stay on your relay.
- **Restarts:** the Docker relay loses buffered frames on restart. Devices reconnect by themselves.

## Push notifications

- The relay sends the APNs pushes. It needs the Worker secrets `APNS_KEY_ID`, `APNS_TEAM_ID` and `APNS_KEY_P8` (`apps/relay/src/apns.ts`). Without them, the relay still forwards frames but wakes nobody. To check the names only, run `wrangler secret list` from `apps/relay`.
- iOS uses production APNs. `UIBackgroundModes: remote-notification` lets the silent push reconnect a suspended app.
- The Mac gets no APNs. While the app runs, a reply in a conversation that is not in front posts a local notification.

## Data paths

Where each side keeps keys, state and cache: [architecture.md](architecture.md#data-on-each-side).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `plugins install` is refused with `Plugin config repair could not be inspected: yorozu …` | OpenClaw's state still holds a pending migration for an older plugin with the id `yorozu`. `openclaw doctor --fix` runs the pending repair, but it rewrites OpenClaw state and also acts on other plugins' pending migrations. |
| `channels status` shows Yorozu `recovering` with `unable to get local issuer certificate` | Node cannot verify the relay's TLS certificate because its OpenSSL has no CA bundle. Restore that OpenSSL's CA bundle, then run `openclaw gateway restart`. |
| `channels status` shows `recovering` with another error | The relay is unreachable. The plugin redials with backoff (up to 30 s) and registers again by itself. |
| The channel stops with `yorozu host key file is malformed` | The host key file is damaged. Restore it from a backup. Deleting it makes a new room, and every device has to pair again. |
| `Configured plugin load path is unavailable: …/plugins/openclaw-yorozu` | The linked directory is gone (for example, a removed worktree). Install again with `--link` from a checkout that exists. |
| `OpenClaw does not know the command "yorozu"` | The plugin is not installed in this profile, or the Gateway has not been restarted since the install. |
| `openclaw yorozu pair` or `devices` cannot connect, or `pair` fails with `the yorozu channel is not connected to its relay` | The Gateway is not running, or the channel is not connected. Check `openclaw channels status`. For a non-default port or a remote Gateway, pass `--port`, or `--url` with `--token`. |
| The app shows "Couldn’t pair", or "Removed from the host" right after pairing | The relay refused the token (`unknown token` or `expired token`: already used, or older than 10 minutes), or the plugin no longer holds the pairing secret (used, expired, or the Gateway restarted). Run `openclaw yorozu pair` again. |
| The app says "Update required" | The client and the plugin share no protocol version. Update the older side. |
| "Edit in Chat" or session tools are refused by the agent | `yorozu:owner` is not in `commands.ownerAllowFrom` ([Owner-only tools](#owner-only-tools)). |

sections.heading: Setup
sections.text: How to put Yorozu on an OpenClaw Gateway, pair a device and chat, plus what building the client needs. Run the OpenClaw commands below on the computer that runs the Gateway, from the repository root of the main checkout. The parts are described in [architecture.md](architecture.md), and the plugin's behaviour in [its README](../plugins/openclaw-yorozu/README.md).

sections.heading: Tools
sections.text:
| Need | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| OpenClaw | 2026.9.8 or later (`peerDependencies` in `plugins/openclaw-yorozu/package.json`) | The `openclaw` CLI on `PATH` and a running Gateway. The Gateway loads the plugin's TypeScript from source; there is no build step. |
| Xcode | 27 (CI uses 27.1) | Builds the client (`apps/ios`) and `packages/YorozuWire`. |
| Tuist | pinned in `mise.toml` | Install with `mise install`. The generated Xcode project and workspace are gitignored. |
| Upload tools | system | `scripts/upload_ios.sh` also uses `openssl`, `curl`, `jq`, `awk` and `xxd`. |

sections.heading: 1. Install the plugin
sections.text:
```sh
openclaw plugins install --link plugins/openclaw-yorozu --force --accept-capabilities
openclaw gateway restart
openclaw channels status
```

- `--link` loads the plugin from this directory, and code changes load on the next Gateway restart. Link from a checkout that stays, not from a worktree that will be removed.
- `--force` accepts a source that is not on ClawHub. `--accept-capabilities` gives the capability consent that the install otherwise stops to ask for.
- No `channels.yorozu` entry is needed, because every key has a default ([Config](#2-config)).
- On first start the plugin makes its host keys. The Gateway log shows `yorozu started (agent <agent>, room <room id>)`, then `yorozu: registered at relay, room <room id>`, and `openclaw channels status` shows the Yorozu channel connected.
- The Mac app also carries a copy of the plugin at `Yorozu.app/Contents/Resources/openclaw-channel`. A Gateway linked there runs the plugin version of the installed app.

The `openclaw yorozu` commands reach the running plugin through Gateway methods, so the Gateway must be running with the channel connected. They accept the usual Gateway client options (`--url`, `--port`, `--token`, `--password`, `--timeout`).

To try the plugin without touching a Gateway in use, run it in an isolated OpenClaw profile ([plugin README](../plugins/openclaw-yorozu/README.md#trying-it-without-the-main-gateway)).

sections.heading: 2. Config
sections.text:
Every key under `channels.yorozu` is optional:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `channels.yorozu.enabled` | `true` | `false` stops the channel |
| `channels.yorozu.agent` | `main` | The agent that answers every Yorozu conversation, and whose cron jobs the Automations tab lists |
| `channels.yorozu.relayUrl` | `wss://relay.yumi.to` | The relay that the plugin and the apps meet on. It goes into the pairing link. |
| `channels.yorozu.mediaMaxMb` | `agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb`, else 128 | Attachment size limit, both ways |
| `channels.yorozu.textChunkLimit` | 4000 | Longest reply chunk, in characters |

```sh
openclaw config set channels.yorozu.agent <agent id>
```

The plugin declares `channels.yorozu` as its reload prefix, so OpenClaw restarts the channel when that config changes. Changing `relayUrl` moves the host to another relay, so every device has to pair again.

sections.heading: Owner-only tools
sections.text:
OpenClaw treats a Yorozu turn as a non-owner sender, so its owner-only agent tools are denied. That includes `automations`, which the Automations tab's "Edit in Chat" needs. To give Yorozu turns owner authority, add `yorozu:owner` to `commands.ownerAllowFrom` and keep the entries already there:

```sh
openclaw config get commands.ownerAllowFrom
openclaw config set commands.ownerAllowFrom '[<existing entries>, "yorozu:owner"]' --strict-json
```

This gives every paired device the owner's authority over the agent.

sections.heading: OpenClaw updates
sections.text:
Yorozu does not update OpenClaw. OpenClaw's own auto-update does it: when the Gateway is idle, it drains running turns, updates, restarts and checks the result, and rolls back if that fails. Meanwhile the apps show the Gateway as offline. Auto-update needs both of these:

- `update.auto.enabled` set to `true` (it is off by default), with `update.checkOnStart` not `false` and `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` not set:

  ```sh
  openclaw config set update.auto.enabled true
  ```

- The Gateway running as a managed service (launchd, systemd or a Scheduled Task). A Gateway started in a terminal only logs that an update is available:

  ```sh
  openclaw gateway install
  ```

If either is missing, the plugin posts a notice into the most recent conversation after the Gateway starts. It posts it again only when what is missing changes. After an update, it posts `Updated OpenClaw <old> → <new>` there once ([plugin README](../plugins/openclaw-yorozu/README.md#gateway-notices-srcupdatests)). OpenClaw's own guide: `docs/install/updating/automatic-updates.md` in the OpenClaw source.

sections.heading: Models
sections.text: Yorozu has no model settings of its own; it uses the configured agent's models. Titles come from OpenClaw's title generator, which uses the agent's utility model first and then its primary model. Attachments reach the model as media, so pictures need a model that accepts image input.

sections.heading: 3. Install a client
sections.text:
- **iPhone, iPad**: the Yorozu app from TestFlight or the App Store ([release.md](release.md#ios-and-ipados-testflight)).
- **Mac**: `scripts/build_native.sh` builds the client into `/Applications/Yorozu.app` ([release.md](release.md#mac-local-build)).

The app and the plugin speak the same wire; old clients keep working ([contract](ios-relay-contract.md#frames)).

sections.heading: 4. Pair a device
sections.text:
```sh
openclaw yorozu pair
```

The command prints a QR code, a `yorozu://pair?…` link, the host fingerprint and the expiry time. The code works for one device, within 10 minutes, and only until the next Gateway restart.

1. In the app, on "Pair with your host", do one of these:
   - On iPhone or iPad, tap Scan QR Code and scan the code.
   - On any device, paste the link (or the https link the QR encodes) with Paste, or type it into "Pairing link" and tap Pair.
2. The app asks "Pair with this host?" and shows the host key. Pair only if it matches the fingerprint the command printed.
3. Pairing is done when the conversation list appears and `openclaw yorozu devices` lists the device by its model name. The app then asks to allow notifications.

**From a paired device:** Settings › Add a Device… makes a fresh pairing code on the host and shows it as a QR code and a link.

**A new Mac from a paired iPhone or iPad:** the Mac's pairing screen shows a code, which changes every 10 minutes.

1. On the iPhone or iPad, open Settings › Add a Device › Scan a Mac's Code (or point the Camera at the code) and tap Add.
2. On the Mac, check that the host key matches and click Pair.

Pair each device separately; all of them see the same conversations. At most 16 devices can be paired: a 17th replaces the oldest.

sections.heading: Try demo data without a host
sections.text:
On the pairing screen, enter `YOROZU-DEMO` in **Pairing link** and tap **Pair**, or scan a QR code containing that text. Surrounding whitespace is ignored, and the code is case-sensitive. Demo mode shows sample conversations and automations and gives scripted replies; no host is involved. Settings › **Exit Demo** leaves it, and the existing pairing is kept.

For development, launch with `--demo` to start in demo mode directly. On the Mac, use a dev build with its own bundle id ([release.md](release.md#compile-checks)):

```sh
open -n .build/xcode-mac/Build/Products/Debug/YorozuIOS.app --args --demo
```

On an iOS Simulator with the app installed, run `xcrun simctl launch <udid> to.yumi.yorozu.ios --demo`.

sections.heading: Devices
sections.text:
```sh
openclaw yorozu devices               # id, name, paired at
openclaw yorozu devices remove <id>   # the id, or a unique start of it
```

`remove` takes the device off the allowlist and tells the relay to forget it and close its sockets. The app then shows "Removed from the host". In the app, Settings lists the paired devices, can turn push on or off for each, and can remove other devices. Settings › Unpair This Device removes this device on the host and deletes its keys and cache.

- **Docker** (Node, keeps everything in memory):


docs.text:
# Status

Current state of `main`. Version: SemVer from the Conventional Commits since the last stable tag (`scripts/version.sh`). Product decisions: [OWNER_DECISIONS.md](../OWNER_DECISIONS.md). Release flow: [release.md](release.md).

## Implemented

- **Plugin** (`plugins/openclaw-yorozu`): host keys in the OpenClaw credentials store; relay connection with reconnect; Noise IK handshakes from allowlisted devices; `openclaw yorozu pair`, `devices`, `devices remove`. Text in and out through one OpenClaw thread session per conversation, with `run_started`, typing, `tool` rows and chunked whole replies; cron delivery into a conversation; history from the Gateway transcripts (`conv_list`, `history`); titles, rename, archive, delete; read cursors; attachments both ways (default limit 128 MB; `channels.yorozu.mediaMaxMb`, else `agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb`); replies both ways (reply targets into the turn, `[[reply_to…]]` out); reactions both ways (system events in, the message tool's `react` out); one sealed push per finished reply; read-only cron list; device list and settings; `pair_invite` for adding a Mac.
- **Wire** (`packages/YorozuWire`, plugin `src/wire.ts`/`src/envelope.ts`): [contract](ios-relay-contract.md); the plugin accepts both frame formats.
- **Relay** (`apps/relay`): Cloudflare Worker, one Durable Object per room, one-time pairing mailboxes, APNs sender, connect rate limit; deploys on merge after its tests.
- **Client** (`apps/ios`, one target for iPhone, iPad and native SwiftUI Mac): pairing by QR scan or pasted link with fingerprint check; a new Mac shows a code that a paired iPhone or iPad scans; conversation list, chat, outbox and cache; replies (Reply in the action row and context menu, quote headers that scroll to the target); reactions (React in the action row and context menu, six quick emoji and More… for the system emoji picker, chips on the bubble); unread badges and read marks synced; attachments, paste and camera; share extension and notification service extension (iOS); two conversations side by side (`Pair.swift`); read-only Automations with "Edit in Chat"; Settings (tabs General, Devices, Host and About on the Mac, each sized to its content; one list on iPhone and iPad) with paired devices; About with version, links, Sparkle update settings on the Mac, and Copy Diagnostics (`Diagnostics.swift`: app, device, connection state and this launch’s log, no keys or messages); Add a Device shows when the new device has paired; App Shortcuts; interface in English, Japanese, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Korean, Spanish, French, German and Brazilian Portuguese (the last seven machine-translated); offline demo (`YOROZU-DEMO` in the pairing field, or `--demo`).
- **Mac app**: Developer ID signed, notarized DMG with Sparkle updates (stable and beta feeds), bundled plugin copy.
- **Zoom** (Mac and iPad, `Zoom.swift`): View > Zoom In (⌘+, ⌘=), Zoom Out (⌘−), Actual Size (⌘0) scale the app's text in seven steps from 75% to 200%, stored per device. The iPad shifts the system Dynamic Type size; the Mac, which has no Dynamic Type, scales text-style fonts and its AppKit text views. Window titles, toolbars, menus and pop-up buttons keep the system size on the Mac. The iPhone follows the system text size only.
- **Voice input** (opt-in, iPhone, iPad and Mac; `VoiceSetup.swift`, `VoiceModel.swift`, `VoiceSettings.swift`, `VoiceRecorder.swift`, `VoiceInput.swift`, `Transcriber.swift`, `packages/YorozuVoice`): Settings › Voice Input turns it on; Model picks the engine behind one protocol (`SpeechEngine`), each row with download size, languages, memory needed, streaming and license, a reason when the device can't run it, and Delete for a downloaded model that isn't selected; Licenses links [docs/voice-licenses](voice-licenses/README.md). Engines: Apple Speech (`SpeechAnalyzer`, iOS 26 and macOS 26 or later; the system installs each language, with progress; Automatic is the device's language and the list holds only the languages it supports there), LFM3-Audio-2B (Q4_K_M model and Q8_0 audio projector, 1.44 GB, 18 languages, through llama.cpp b11954 in `packages/Llama`), Whisper Large v3 Turbo (740 MB) and Whisper Small (489 MB), 99 languages, through WhisperKit (argmax-oss-swift 1.1.1), and Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming 0.6B (615 MB, 8 languages, Apple silicon) through FluidAudio 0.18.0. Until the owner picks, Apple Speech is the default where it runs, and a device that had downloaded LFM3-Audio-2B stays on it. Every downloaded model's files are pinned by Hugging Face revision and SHA-256 (`VoiceCatalog.swift`): iPhone and iPad (iOS 26 or later) get one on-demand Apple-hosted asset pack per model (`VoiceModel`, `VoiceWhisperTurbo`, `VoiceWhisperSmall`, `VoiceNemotron`) through the `YorozuAssets` downloader extension ([release.md](release.md#voice-model-asset-packs)), and a model whose pack App Store Connect doesn't have yet shows Not available yet; the Mac downloads into Application Support, excluded from backup, resuming a partial download. The download waits for Wi-Fi (no cellular, hotspot or Low Data Mode) unless Download Using Cellular… is confirmed. Dictionary (Settings › Voice Input › Dictionary, up to 200 words of 64 characters, stored on the device only and kept out of logs and Copy Diagnostics): each word goes to the engine as a hint (Apple's contextual strings, Whisper's prompt, Nemotron's custom vocabulary, an instruction to LFM3-Audio; a hinted LFM3-Audio transcript that repeats a word or phrase three times in a row, is mostly dictionary words or reads back the Vocabulary list is decoded again without hints, and when that one loops too nothing was recognized, `TranscriptDegeneration.swift`; each LFM3-Audio decode stops after 33 tokens a second of audio, at least 128 (three times the fastest speech measured, 10.4 tokens a second), and one that gets there counts as a loop, `TranscriptBudget.swift`), and a word with Heard As replaces that text in every engine's transcript, longest match first, whole words in spaced scripts, ignoring case and width (`VoiceDictionary.swift`, tested with `swift test --package-path packages/YorozuVoice`). The composer's mic (left of Send) records 16 kHz mono up to 5 minutes (`RecordingLimits.maxSeconds`; then "Recording stopped at the 5-minute limit.") with a waveform and timer: ✕ (Esc) cancels, ✓ (Return) inserts the transcript at the caret, send (⌘Return) posts draft and transcript as one message. The engine loads while the owner speaks and transcribes off the main thread; a failure keeps the clip for Retry. Background (iPhone and iPad, the `audio` background mode): recording keeps going when the owner switches apps or locks the phone, with the system's mic indicator; `Dictation.swift` owns one session per conversation, so the composer, the Talk to Yorozu control and the Live Activity drive the same recording. A call or Siri pauses it (Paused, the samples kept) and it resumes when the system says so, else with Resume; losing the input route (AirPods removed) or an engine configuration change restarts the tap on the new input, same clip (`RecordingMachine.swift`, tested). Each clip streams to `VoiceClips/` as it is spoken (`ClipStore.swift`, tested) and stays until its text is in the composer; a clip a killed app left is transcribed into its conversation's composer the next time the app is in front, never sent. Live Activity: a Recording row with Cancel and Stop (`StopRecordingIntent`, `CancelRecordingIntent`; Stop transcribes into the composer, never sends), then Transcribing, then Done (in the background with the Transcript Ready or Recording Stopped alert, plus a local notification that opens the conversation) or Failed. After a stop, per engine (`VoiceEngineID.usesGPU`, `TranscriptionPlan.swift`, tested): Apple Speech (the system's speech service) and Nemotron (Core ML on CPU and Neural Engine) transcribe at once, in the background too, under a background task; Whisper (its mel spectrogram on `.cpuAndGPU`) and LFM3-Audio-2B (llama.cpp on Metal) need the GPU, which iOS denies in the background, so stopped in front on iOS 26 with `BGTaskScheduler.supportedResources` containing `.gpu` they run in a continued-processing task (`to.yumi.yorozu.ios.voice-transcribe.<uuid>`, system progress UI, expiry keeps the clip), stopped in front otherwise they run in front, and stopped in the background (Lock Screen Stop, the 5-minute limit) or failing there they wait and transcribe when the app comes forward. Measured on an M4 Mac mini with six synthetic English and six synthetic Japanese clips (two system voices each; word error rate for English, 64 words, character error rate for Japanese, 146 characters; raw, then with a dictionary of hints and Heard As fixes): LFM3-Audio-2B English 10.9%, 0.0% with the dictionary, Japanese right on one voice and looping or empty on the other (52% with the dictionary; with the retry, six regenerated Japanese clips gave 12.2% and 9.8% with the dictionary and no loop, and slowed, noise-only, silent or humming audio, where hinted LFM3-Audio read the dictionary back, gave a short phrase or nothing; 8 s of silence that looped to the end of the context took 132 s, and 5.4 s with the token budget); Whisper Large v3 Turbo English 10.9%, 1.6%, Japanese 4.1%, 0.0%, about 0.5 s a clip after a 121 s first load (Core ML compiles once); Whisper Small English 10.9%, 1.6%, Japanese 24.7%, 15.1%; Nemotron 3.5 ASR English 10.9%, 3.1%, Japanese 17.1%, 17.1%, about 0.1 s a clip; Apple Speech English 10.9%, 4.7%, Japanese 4.1%, 1.4% (its contextual strings changed nothing). LFM3-Audio-2B alone: 27 s of English speech in about 2 s, model load 0.2–5 s (cold), peak footprint about 0.8 GB with 1.9 GB resident including the mapped weights.
- **Widgets, controls and Live Activity** (iPhone and iPad, iOS 18 or later; `YorozuWidgets` extension, `Sources/WidgetShared`, `WidgetPublisher.swift`, `YorozuActivities.swift`): the app and the notification service write a snapshot to the App Group (`WidgetSnapshot.json`: up to 12 conversations with title, pinned, unread count and last reply time, the total unread count as on the badge, the accent, and the latest reply's first line only while Settings › Show Message Previews in Widgets is on, off by default), atomically, only when it changed, then reload the widgets; demo mode writes none (its taps open only new conversations, Ask and Talk) and unpairing deletes it. Conversations widget (small, medium, large; medium and large chosen per widget from the snapshot) with pinned then recent rows, unread dots, relative times, a tap opening the conversation, + (new conversation) and Ask (new conversation, keyboard up). Lock Screen accessories: circular (unread count or glyph), rectangular (latest conversation and count), inline ("2 new replies, latest: Trip planning"). Lock Screen launcher (circular, no snapshot read): Ask, the Yorozu mark alone (new conversation, keyboard up). Control Center: New Conversation and Talk to Yorozu (new conversation with voice input, or the voice setup when the model isn't ready). Titles and previews are privacy-sensitive (hidden on a locked screen); counts stay. Live Activity (Settings › Show Live Activity, on by default, the same `turnLiveActivity` key as before): one device-local activity for the whole app (`YorozuActivityAttributes`), whose state is a list of at most 8 jobs (turn, recording, transcribing, needs you; running, done or failed; a tool step count and times), each keyed by a random token and never by a conversation. What a token is about (the conversation to open, and its title only while widget previews are on) is in `ActivityLabels.json` beside the widget snapshot, written by the app and the notification service and pruned to the live tokens; the views read it at render time and show a title only while previews are on, else "Working", "Recording", "Transcribing", "Needs you", "Done" or "Failed"; never message text, tool names or arguments. Lock Screen and expanded Dynamic Island: up to 3 rows (needs you, recording, running, finished; newest first) plus "+N more", each opening its conversation (a token without a label opens the app); compact: the mark, and "!" for needs you, else a pulsing mic while recording, else the running count; minimal: the mark with that badge. Turns from the in-app watcher start it when the app leaves the foreground (ActivityKit can't start one from the background); recording and transcription start it in the app and keep it on return, while returning otherwise ends it; a running recording row adds Cancel and Stop buttons, which act in the app without opening it. Finished rows linger 2 minutes; with nothing running and nobody left to clear them, it ends and the system dismisses it then; no jobs, no activity; a stale date marks 15 minutes without an update. The notification service updates it silently: a reply marks the turn done and drops its approval row, a failure marks it failed, an approval adds a needs-you row (it can't start an activity). It alerts only for events no push announces: a transcript ready, the recording limit, a send the relay refused. With a plugin listing `liveActivityPush` (its relay has an APNs key), the activity takes a push token and the app reports it, its jobs and each running turn's conversation over the encrypted session; the plugin then pushes counts-only states through the relay while the app is suspended (tool steps at most every 15 s at priority 5, a finished turn at once at priority 10, never an alert; `end` when nothing runs), passing recording and transcription rows through unchanged. docs.title: UI layout
docs.text:
# UI layout

Let the platform decide sizes. Take widths, heights and spacing from the container or the
system; a number chosen on one device is wrong on the next. The client in `apps/ios` is one
SwiftUI app for iPhone, iPad and Mac (native macOS, not Catalyst), so every layout runs on
all three.

## Rule

Use the native mechanism first, in this order:

1. The container's proposal. A navigation bar, toolbar, list row, or stack already offers a
   view the room it has. Take it: `frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`, `lineLimit`, `truncationMode`.
2. Adaptive layout views. `ViewThatFits`, `Layout`, `containerRelativeFrame`, size classes,
   `dynamicTypeSize`, `safeAreaInset`, `scrollTargetLayout`.
3. Measuring. `onGeometryChange(for:of:)` or `GeometryReader` when a view must react to
   the size it was actually given; compare against that size.

Hard-coded points, `fixedSize` on something that lives inside a system container, or a
`frame(width:)`/`frame(maxWidth:)` picked by eye are all guesses about a bar the system
draws. They break on a narrower device, a larger type size, a split view, or the next OS.

## Exception

A custom component owns its own geometry. Fixed sizes belong there when they are the
design: spacing inside a card, a corner radius, a send button's circle. Keep each as one
named constant, and still let the component's outer size come from its container.

## Check the proposal exists

Native sizing only works when the container actually proposes a size. Some do not: a
Mac window proposes no size, and a custom `.principal` toolbar view is laid
out at its ideal width rather than the room left in the bar. Before building on a proposal,
confirm it on each target device: `onGeometryChange` and a `print` of the frame settle it.
Where the platform withholds the width, use the platform view that has it (the system title).

## Text

Fonts are text styles only, set with `textStyle(_:weight:monospaced:)` from `Zoom.swift` rather than `font(_:)`:
on the Mac it applies the app's zoom (⌘+ / ⌘−), which `dynamicTypeSize` does not reach there. A size that
grows with text uses `@ScaledMetric` times the `textZoom` environment value. A view that keeps a
system font (a sidebar row, `ContentUnavailableView`) takes `zoomedFont(_:)`.

## Where the constants live

All paths are under `apps/ios/Sources/YorozuIOS/`.

- `LayoutMetrics` in `Metrics.swift` is the shared scale: spacing (`hair` 2 … `section` 24),
  the caps `readingWidth` (700) and `composerWidth` (640), which only an iPad or a Mac window
  reaches, and the corner radii (10 on the Mac, 14 and 16 on iPhone and iPad).
  Mac only: the sidebar column widths and the window's least size (`windowMinWidth`,
  `windowMinHeight`), set in `YorozuApp.swift` because a window proposes no size.
- `controlTarget` in `Metrics.swift` is the one size that differs by input: 44 points on
  iPhone and iPad, 28 on the Mac. Chat controls take their size from it, not from literals.
- `MarkdownMetrics` in `ChatMarkdown.swift` holds the message renderer's spacing, insets and
  radius; its width always comes from the row. A code block scrolls sideways, a table's cells

sections.heading: UI layout
sections.text:
Let the platform decide sizes. Take widths, heights and spacing from the container or the
system; a number chosen on one device is wrong on the next. The client in `apps/ios` is one
SwiftUI app for iPhone, iPad and Mac (native macOS, not Catalyst), so every layout runs on
all three.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.text:
Use the native mechanism first, in this order:

1. The container's proposal. A navigation bar, toolbar, list row, or stack already offers a
   view the room it has. Take it: `frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`, `lineLimit`, `truncationMode`.
2. Adaptive layout views. `ViewThatFits`, `Layout`, `containerRelativeFrame`, size classes,
   `dynamicTypeSize`, `safeAreaInset`, `scrollTargetLayout`.
3. Measuring. `onGeometryChange(for:of:)` or `GeometryReader` when a view must react to
   the size it was actually given; compare against that size.

`frame(width:)`/`frame(maxWidth:)` picked by eye are all guesses about a bar the system
draws. They break on a narrower device, a larger type size, a split view, or the next OS.

sections.heading: Exception
sections.text:
A custom component owns its own geometry. Fixed sizes belong there when they are the
design: spacing inside a card, a corner radius, a send button's circle. Keep each as one
named constant, and still let the component's outer size come from its container.

docs.text:
# openclaw-yorozu

The OpenClaw channel plugin `yorozu`. It holds the host keys and one outbound WebSocket to the relay, answers wire handshakes from allowlisted devices ([docs/ios-relay-contract.md](../../docs/ios-relay-contract.md)), and runs one agent turn per incoming message. Install, config keys, pairing and troubleshooting: [docs/setup.md](../../docs/setup.md). The OpenClaw SDK surface it relies on: [docs/openclaw-channel.md](../../docs/openclaw-channel.md).

## Entry points

- `index.ts`: the channel entry, the `openclaw yorozu` CLI registration, and the Gateway methods below (all scope `operator.admin`).
- `setup-entry.ts`: the setup entry (`defineSetupPluginEntry`).
- `openclaw.plugin.json`: plugin id `yorozu`, channel `yorozu`, CLI command `yorozu`, and the `channels.yorozu` schema.

| Gateway method | Params | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `yorozu.pair.begin` | none | `openclaw yorozu pair` |
| `yorozu.devices.list` | none | `openclaw yorozu devices` |
| `yorozu.devices.remove` | `{id}`: full key or a unique prefix | `openclaw yorozu devices remove` |

A method fails with `UNAVAILABLE` and the error text, for example while the channel is not connected to its relay.

## Relay host (`src/relay.ts`, `src/wire.ts`, `src/envelope.ts`)

- Connects to `<relayUrl>?room=<room id>`, registers by signing the relay's nonce, then sends the device allowlist (`devices`). Pings every 30 s and drops a half-open socket. Redials with backoff from 1 s up to 30 s until the account stops.
- A handshake is answered only when the device's Ed25519 key and the X25519 key its handshake authenticates both match an allowlist row, or when it proves a pending pairing. Anything else gets a `revoke` to the relay. A handshake id that was already answered is not answered again within the 5-minute freshness window.
- One session per device, in memory. Sessions survive relay reconnects but not a channel or Gateway restart.
- Each device must send `peer_info` before anything else counts. If the protocol versions do not overlap, the device gets `error update_required` and its session is dropped. The host's `peer_info` carries the agent, the OpenClaw version, `mediaMaxBytes` and the capabilities `attachments`, `devices`, `invite`, `replies` and `reactions`, plus `liveActivityPush` while the relay can push.
- Frames the relay buffered (`seq`) are acked after handling. Host frames are batched at up to 16 frames and under 1 MiB per batch.

## Keys and devices (`src/keys.ts`, `src/devices.ts`)

- **Host keys**: an X25519 static key and an Ed25519 relay key, made on first start in `<OpenClaw credentials dir>/yorozu/host-keys.json` (`resolveOAuthDir()`, written with `createSecretFileAtomic`) and never rewritten. The room id is `base64url(sha256(Ed25519 public key))`. It is logged at start and on every registration; keys are never logged. A malformed file stops the channel rather than being replaced. Deleting the file makes a new room, and every device has to pair again.
- **Allowlist**: rows in the plugin's keyed state store (namespace `devices`), keyed by the device's Ed25519 key, with its X25519 key, model name (from `peer_info`), paired time and push flag. At most 16 devices; past that the oldest is removed and revoked at the relay.

## Pairing

- `pair`: the plugin asks the relay for a one-time join token (`mint`) and makes a 32-byte secret. The secret is kept in memory until the token expires. It returns `yorozu://pair?v=3&relay=…&key=…&token=…&room=…&secret=…`, the same query as the fragment of `https://yorozu.yumi.to/pair#…` (which is what the QR carries), the host fingerprint and the expiry. The CLI writes to stdout directly, because OpenClaw's console capture redacts key- and token-like text.
- Joining: when a handshake's `helloProof` matches a pending secret, the device is added and the secret is dropped. A Gateway restart forgets pending secrets.
- `pair_invite` from a paired device gets a fresh code made the same way, so a device can be added away from the host.
- Removal (`devices remove`, or `device_patch {removed}` from Settings): the row is deleted, the session is dropped, and the relay gets `revoke`. If the relay is unreachable at that moment, the next registration's `devices` list has the same effect.

## Conversations (`src/conversation.ts`)

Every device is the same channel peer, `owner`. A conversation is the session `<owner session>:thread:<convId>`, where `<owner session>` is the key OpenClaw routes the peer to: `agent:<agent>:yorozu:direct:owner` by default, with `<agent>` from `channels.yorozu.agent`, but `bindings` and `session.identityLinks` can change the agent or the peer part, so the plugin resolves it at start (`setThreadBase`).

- **In**: a `message` is answered `delivered` to every device at once. A repeated `messageId` gets `delivered` again but does not run twice (remembered for 24 h). The message's uploaded files become media facts, and the turn runs through `runChannelInboundEvent` with commands authorized. Slash commands pass through as text; OpenClaw handles `/new` for that thread only.
- **Out**, to every device with a live session: `run_started`, then `typing` (repeated every 8 s), then `tool` per tool call (`running`, then `done` or `failed`), then one `reply` per chunk of the text chunk limit. Media goes on the last chunk as `attachments`. A failure sends `error run_failed`. Nothing is queued for offline devices; `history` serves the reply from the transcript later.
- **Retries** (`src/retry.ts`): a run that fails with a temporary error (plugin reload, overload, rate limit, 429/503/529, connection reset) before any reply or tool call is parked in the keyed state store (namespace `retry`). It runs again after 5, 15, 30, 60 and 120 s, and only the last failure is shown. A generation that replaces this one after a reload picks up the parked runs.
- **Replies** (`src/replies.ts`): a `message`'s `replyTo` reaches the turn as OpenClaw's quote context (`ReplyToId`, `ReplyToBody`). The channel's reply mode is `off`, so only an explicit `[[reply_to…]]` tag or the message tool's `replyTo` gives an outbound `replyToId`; the plugin turns it into the `reply`'s `replyTo`, with the target's text from the turn or the transcript. Each `replyTo` is kept by the replying message's id (namespace `replies`) for its history item.
- **Reactions** (`src/reactions.ts`): one emoji per person per message. A device's `reaction` updates the user's slot, goes to every device, and queues the system event `Yorozu reaction added: <emoji> on msg <id>` (or `removed`) in the conversation's session, replacing a pending one for that message; it does not start a turn. The agent reacts through the `message` tool's `react` action (`plugin.actions`; `capabilities.reactions`, `reactionSlots: "single"`), which updates the agent's slot and sends `reaction` with `by: "agent"`. Reactions are kept by message id (namespace `reactions`) for history items.
- **Deliveries from outside a turn** (cron): the outbound adapter's `sendText` and `sendMedia` send a `reply` into the conversation named by the delivery's `threadId`, with `to: "owner"`. `resolveOutboundSessionRoute` maps it to the thread session, so OpenClaw mirrors the text into that transcript.

## Gateway notices (`src/updates.ts`)

Yorozu never updates OpenClaw itself; it relies on OpenClaw's auto-update ([setup.md](../../docs/setup.md#openclaw-updates)). Each time the channel starts, the plugin may post up to two notices into the most recent unarchived conversation. Each goes out through `sendDurableMessageBatch` with a transcript mirror, so a device that connects later finds it in history. With no conversation yet, nothing is posted.

- **Version**: the OpenClaw version (`runtime.version`) is kept in the keyed state store (namespace `gateway`, key `version`). When it differs from the one stored at the last start, the plugin posts `Updated OpenClaw <old> → <new>` once. The first start only stores it.
- **Auto-update**: the plugin checks what OpenClaw's auto-updater checks: `update.auto.enabled` is `true`, `update.checkOnStart` is not `false`, `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` is not set, and the Gateway runs as the service `openclaw gateway install` made (`OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=openclaw` and `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_KIND=gateway` in its environment). If any check fails, it posts one notice that names each failing check and how to fix it. The list of failures is stored (key `auto-update`), and the notice is posted again only when that list changes. Once every check passes, the stored list is cleared.

## History (`src/history.ts`, `src/activity.ts`)

- `conv_list` and `history` are answered to the asking device only. They are read from the session store and the transcript (`listSessionEntries`, `getSessionEntry`, `loadTranscriptEventsSync`, `readTranscriptStatsSync`), never from `chat.history`. Pages hold up to 60 items and 192 KiB; one item's text is cut at 60,000 characters (the transcript keeps the whole text). Built item lists are cached for the 8 most recent sessions.
- Live replies take their ids from the transcript message they came from, so a device does not show a reply twice after paging.
- **Message times**: `conv_list`'s `updatedAt` is the conversation's newest user or agent message time from its transcript. It is kept per transcript revision in the keyed state store (namespace `message-times`).

## Titles, rename, pin, archive, delete (`src/sessions.ts`)

- After a turn, a conversation with neither `label` nor `displayName` gets a title. It comes from `generateConversationLabel` on its first non-command user message and is written as `displayName`, with at most 60 characters.
- `conv_patch`:
  - `title` sets `label` (an empty title clears it); `label` wins over `displayName`.
  - `archived` sets or clears `archivedAt`; archiving also clears `pinnedAt`.
  - `pinned` sets or clears `pinnedAt`. An archived conversation cannot be pinned.
  - `deleted` archives the conversation, then `deleteSessionEntry` with the transcript archived, and drops its read cursor.
  - All writes keep the entry's activity time (`preserveActivity`).
- The plugin watches session changes (`subscribeSessionChanges`) and sends every device a `conv_update` when a conversation's title, archive or pin state changed, whoever changed it.

## Read marks, push, automations, attachments, settings

- **Read marks** (`src/reads.ts`): one cursor per conversation (namespace `read`). It only moves forward, is broadcast to every device, and goes to each device when its session opens.
- **Push** (`src/push.ts`): one relay `notify` per finished reply, including cron deliveries with text. It is sealed per device (title and first line, 256 bytes at most). It goes to every paired device except those with push off and those whose live session reports the app in front or this conversation open. When a device reads a conversation, the other devices alerted for it get a silent `notify` of class `sync`.
- **Live Activity push** (`src/liveactivity.ts`, wired in `src/relay.ts` and `src/conversation.ts`): capability `liveActivityPush`, listed only while the relay's `registered` says `liveActivity: true`. A device's `live_activity` report (push token, jobs, running turn → conversation) is kept in memory and its token sent to the relay (`activityToken`). Tool calls and the end of a turn change only that turn's job; the whole state goes to the relay as `activityPush`, steps at priority 5 at most once per 15 s, finished rows at priority 10, `end` when nothing runs. Other jobs pass through unchanged. Details: [Live Activity push](../../docs/ios-relay-contract.md#live-activity-push).
- **Automations** (`src/cron.ts`): `cron_list` is answered with every job of the configured agent, including disabled ones. A job without `agentId` counts for the system agent, or else the default agent. Each job comes with its schedule in English words, next and last run, last status and error, and its Yorozu conversation when it delivers into one. The list is read from the cron store with `loadCronStore`. If that fails, the answer carries `error`. Yorozu only reads the jobs.
- **Attachments** (`src/attachments.ts`, `src/spool.ts`): uploads arrive in chunks, spooled to disk so they resume after a reconnect or restart (`upload_status`, capability `resume`), then go into OpenClaw's media store, indexed in the keyed state store (namespace `attachments`). Outbound media is staged and announced in the `reply`, and each device downloads it on request, sealed for that device. The size limit is the media limit in [setup.md](../../docs/setup.md#2-config).
- **Settings**: `device_list` lists the paired devices (key, model, paired time, push, and which one is asking). `device_patch` turns push on or off for a device, or removes it.

## Trying it without the main Gateway

An OpenClaw profile keeps its own state, config and port (`~/.openclaw-<name>`). From the repository root:

```sh
openclaw --profile yorozu-dev config set gateway.mode local
openclaw --profile yorozu-dev plugins install --link plugins/openclaw-yorozu --force --accept-capabilities
openclaw --profile yorozu-dev gateway run --port 19422     # foreground; Ctrl-C stops it
openclaw --profile yorozu-dev channels status              # another terminal
openclaw --profile yorozu-dev yorozu pair
```

Use `gateway run`, not `gateway install`, which would add a login service for the profile.

## Typecheck

`tsconfig.json` extends `node_modules/openclaw/tsconfig.json`, so link the OpenClaw source checkout behind the `openclaw` command first (`node_modules/` is git-ignored):

```sh
cd plugins/openclaw-yorozu
mkdir -p node_modules
ln -s "$(dirname "$(realpath "$(command -v openclaw)")")" node_modules/openclaw
node_modules/openclaw/node_modules/.bin/tsc -p . | grep -E '^(index|setup-entry|src/)'
```

No output means the plugin typechecks. The `grep` drops errors from inside the OpenClaw checkout.

## Tests

`src/liveactivity.ts` imports nothing at runtime, so Node runs its tests without OpenClaw: `node --test test/*.test.ts` (Node 26, from this folder). They share `apps/ios/Tests/Fixtures/activity-content-state.json` with the relay's and the app's tests.

Each goes out through `sendDurableMessageBatch` with a transcript mirror, so a device that connects later finds it in history. With no conversation yet, nothing is posted.

- **Version**: the OpenClaw version (`runtime.version`) is kept in the keyed state store (namespace `gateway`, key `version`). When it differs from the one stored at the last start, the plugin posts `Updated OpenClaw <old> → <new>` once. The first start only stores it.
- **Auto-update**: the plugin checks what OpenClaw's auto-updater checks: `update.auto.enabled` is `true`, `update.checkOnStart` is not `false`, `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` is not set, and the Gateway runs as the service `openclaw gateway install` made (`OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=openclaw` and `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_KIND=gateway` in its environment). If any check fails, it posts one notice that names each failing check and how to fix it. The list of failures is stored (key `auto-update`), and the notice is posted again only when that list changes. Once every check passes, the stored list is cleared.

sections.heading: History (`src/history.ts`, `src/activity.ts`)
sections.text:
- `conv_list` and `history` are answered to the asking device only. They are read from the session store and the transcript (`listSessionEntries`, `getSessionEntry`, `loadTranscriptEventsSync`, `readTranscriptStatsSync`), never from `chat.history`. Pages hold up to 60 items and 192 KiB; one item's text is cut at 60,000 characters (the transcript keeps the whole text). Built item lists are cached for the 8 most recent sessions.
- Live replies take their ids from the transcript message they came from, so a device does not show a reply twice after paging.
- **Message times**: `conv_list`'s `updatedAt` is the conversation's newest user or agent message time from its transcript. It is kept per transcript revision in the keyed state store (namespace `message-times`).

sections.heading: Titles, rename, pin, archive, delete (`src/sessions.ts`)
sections.text:
- After a turn, a conversation with neither `label` nor `displayName` gets a title. It comes from `generateConversationLabel` on its first non-command user message and is written as `displayName`, with at most 60 characters.
- `conv_patch`:
  - `title` sets `label` (an empty title clears it); `label` wins over `displayName`.
  - `archived` sets or clears `archivedAt`; archiving also clears `pinnedAt`.
  - `pinned` sets or clears `pinnedAt`. An archived conversation cannot be pinned.
  - `deleted` archives the conversation, then `deleteSessionEntry` with the transcript archived, and drops its read cursor.
  - All writes keep the entry's activity time (`preserveActivity`).
- The plugin watches session changes (`subscribeSessionChanges`) and sends every device a `conv_update` when a conversation's title, archive or pin state changed, whoever changed it.

sections.heading: Read marks, push, automations, attachments, settings
sections.text:
- **Read marks** (`src/reads.ts`): one cursor per conversation (namespace `read`). It only moves forward, is broadcast to every device, and goes to each device when its session opens.
- **Push** (`src/push.ts`): one relay `notify` per finished reply, including cron deliveries with text. It is sealed per device (title and first line, 256 bytes at most). It goes to every paired device except those with push off and those whose live session reports the app in front or this conversation open. When a device reads a conversation, the other devices alerted for it get a silent `notify` of class `sync`.
- **Live Activity push** (`src/liveactivity.ts`, wired in `src/relay.ts` and `src/conversation.ts`): capability `liveActivityPush`, listed only while the relay's `registered` says `liveActivity: true`. A device's `live_activity` report (push token, jobs, running turn → conversation) is kept in memory and its token sent to the relay (`activityToken`). Tool calls and the end of a turn change only that turn's job; the whole state goes to the relay as `activityPush`, steps at priority 5 at most once per 15 s, finished rows at priority 10, `end` when nothing runs. Other jobs pass through unchanged. Details: [Live Activity push](../../docs/ios-relay-contract.md#live-activity-push).
- **Automations** (`src/cron.ts`): `cron_list` is answered with every job of the configured agent, including disabled ones. A job without `agentId` counts for the system agent, or else the default agent. Each job comes with its schedule in English words, next and last run, last status and error, and its Yorozu conversation when it delivers into one. The list is read from the cron store with `loadCronStore`. If that fails, the answer carries `error`. Yorozu only reads the jobs.
- **Attachments** (`src/attachments.ts`, `src/spool.ts`): uploads arrive in chunks, spooled to disk so they resume after a reconnect or restart (`upload_status`, capability `resume`), then go into OpenClaw's media store, indexed in the keyed state store (namespace `attachments`). Outbound media is staged and announced in the `reply`, and each device downloads it on request, sealed for that device. The size limit is the media limit in [setup.md](../../docs/setup.md#2-config).
- **Settings**: `device_list` lists the paired devices (key, model, paired time, push, and which one is asking). `device_patch` turns push on or off for a device, or removes it.

sections.heading: Trying it without the main Gateway
sections.text:
An OpenClaw profile keeps its own state, config and port (`~/.openclaw-<name>`). From the repository root:

```sh
openclaw --profile yorozu-dev config set gateway.mode local
openclaw --profile yorozu-dev plugins install --link plugins/openclaw-yorozu --force --accept-capabilities
openclaw --profile yorozu-dev gateway run --port 19422     # foreground; Ctrl-C stops it
openclaw --profile yorozu-dev channels status              # another terminal
openclaw --profile yorozu-dev yorozu pair
```

Use `gateway run`, not `gateway install`, which would add a login service for the profile.

sections.heading: Typecheck
sections.text:
`tsconfig.json` extends `node_modules/openclaw/tsconfig.json`, so link the OpenClaw source checkout behind the `openclaw` command first (`node_modules/` is git-ignored):

```sh
cd plugins/openclaw-yorozu
mkdir -p node_modules
ln -s "$(dirname "$(realpath "$(command -v openclaw)")")" node_modules/openclaw
node_modules/openclaw/node_modules/.bin/tsc -p . | grep -E '^(index|setup-entry|src/)'
```

No output means the plugin typechecks. The `grep` drops errors from inside the OpenClaw checkout.

sections.heading: Tests
sections.text: `src/liveactivity.ts` imports nothing at runtime, so Node runs its tests without OpenClaw: `node --test test/*.test.ts` (Node 26, from this folder). They share `apps/ios/Tests/Fixtures/activity-content-state.json` with the relay's and the app's tests.
