app.description: Off: Return sends a one-line message, Shift-Return adds a new line, and ⌘Return always sends. On: Return adds a new line and only ⌘Return sends.

app.description: Plays a light haptic when a reply in another conversation shows as a notice at the top of the screen while Yorozu is open.

app.title: Show Conversations in Siri and Search
app.description: Lets Siri and Spotlight find conversations by their titles and recent messages. The index stays on the device and is removed when you unpair. Not shown in demo mode.

app.title: Show Live Activity
app.description: On by default. One Live Activity on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island follows the agent's turns, approvals waiting for you, and voice recording and transcription: up to three rows, each opening its conversation, with the tool step count and elapsed time. It shows conversation titles only while message previews are on, and never message text or tool details. It starts when you leave Yorozu with something running, ends when you return (unless a recording or transcription is running), keeps finished rows for about two minutes, and runs on the device only (no push).

app.title: Dictionary
app.description: Names and words voice input gets wrong, up to 200, each with an optional Heard As. Every model is told to expect the words (Apple Speech's contextual strings, Whisper's prompt, Nemotron's custom vocabulary, LFM3-Audio's instruction), and wherever a transcript has a Heard As, the word replaces it, whole words only in spaced languages. The dictionary stays on the device and isn't in Copy Diagnostics.

app.title: Voice Input
app.description: Speak a message instead of typing it. Speech is transcribed on the device by the engine chosen under Model. With Apple Speech (the default on iOS 26 and macOS 26 and later) turning it on has the system download the language; with a downloaded model it downloads that model: from Apple as an asset pack on iPhone and iPad (iOS 26 or later), from Hugging Face on the Mac.

app.title: Model
app.description: The speech engine voice input uses, each listed with its download size, languages, the memory it needs, whether it streams, and its license: Apple Speech (built into iOS 26 and macOS 26; languages vary by device), LFM3-Audio-2B (about 1.44 GB, 18 languages, 6 GB of RAM), Whisper Large v3 Turbo (about 740 MB, 99 languages, 6 GB), Whisper Small (about 490 MB, 99 languages, 4 GB) and Nemotron 3.5 ASR (about 615 MB, 8 languages, 4 GB, streaming; Apple silicon on the Mac). A model whose iPhone and iPad asset pack isn't in App Store Connect yet shows Not available yet. Until you pick one, Apple Speech is used where it runs, and a device that already downloaded LFM3-Audio-2B keeps it. Delete removes a downloaded model that isn't selected. Licenses opens the license texts.

app.title: Language
app.description: The spoken language for voice input, each named in its own language: Automatic, or one of the languages the chosen model supports. Automatic detects the language with the downloaded models; with Apple Speech it uses the device's language, and the list shows only the languages Apple Speech supports on the device.

app.title: Show Message Previews in Widgets
app.description: Off by default. Widgets and Lock Screen accessories show conversation titles, unread counts and reply times, hidden on the Lock Screen until the device is unlocked. On: the medium and large widgets also show the first line of the latest reply. The snapshot stays in the app's App Group container on the device and is deleted when you unpair.

The relay that the plugin and the apps meet on. It goes into the pairing link.

troubleshooting.symptom: The app shows "Can’t reach the relay. Retrying…" or the status "Offline"
troubleshooting.fix: The device can't reach the relay (wss://relay.yumi.to, or the relayUrl the host was paired with). Check the device's internet connection, VPN or firewall. The app retries by itself; messages you send wait in the outbox. With a self-hosted relay, check that it is running and reachable over wss:// (ws:// works only for localhost).

troubleshooting.symptom: The app shows "OpenClaw Gateway is offline. Messages will send when it’s back." or the status "Host offline"
troubleshooting.fix: The relay is reachable but the OpenClaw Gateway with the Yorozu plugin isn't connected to it. On the computer that runs the Gateway, check `openclaw gateway status` and `openclaw channels status`; start or restart it with `openclaw gateway restart`. The banner also shows briefly while OpenClaw updates itself and restarts. Messages sent meanwhile go out when the Gateway is back.

troubleshooting.symptom: The app shows "The agent hasn’t responded in 5 minutes."
troubleshooting.fix: A turn started but the agent has sent nothing for 5 minutes. Check the Gateway's log and the agent's model provider (rate limits, an expired key, a long tool call). Yorozu only carries messages; the agent runs in OpenClaw.

troubleshooting.symptom: Voice input says "The voice model isn’t available for this version of Yorozu yet. Try again later."
troubleshooting.fix: On iPhone and iPad each voice model is an Apple-hosted asset pack (IDs VoiceModel, VoiceWhisperTurbo, VoiceWhisperSmall and VoiceNemotron); Settings › Voice Input › Model shows such a model as Not available yet. Until App Store Connect has processed the pack (and, for the App Store and external TestFlight, approved it), the system knows no pack with that ID (ManagedBackgroundAssetsError.assetPackNotFound). Nothing on the device fixes it: pick another model, tap Try Again later, or update the app. Copy Diagnostics (Settings › About) includes the underlying error.

troubleshooting.symptom: The voice model download says "Waiting for Wi-Fi"
troubleshooting.fix: The download waits for Wi-Fi and doesn't use cellular, a personal hotspot or Low Data Mode. Join Wi-Fi, or tap Download Using Cellular… and confirm.

troubleshooting.symptom: Voice input is greyed out: "Voice input needs iOS 26 or later." or "This device needs more memory for voice input."
troubleshooting.fix: Voice input needs iOS 26 or later on iPhone and iPad (Apple Speech and the Apple-hosted asset packs). On a Mac before macOS 26, or a device where Apple Speech isn't available, a downloaded model is needed: 4 GB of RAM for Whisper Small and Nemotron 3.5 ASR, 6 GB for the others. Settings › Voice Input › Model says why a model can't be picked. Update the OS if the device supports it; otherwise use the system keyboard's dictation.

troubleshooting.symptom: The voice model download fails: interrupted, damaged, or an HTTP error
troubleshooting.fix: Tap Try Again. On the Mac the model comes from Hugging Face, pinned to a revision, and resumes a partial download; a damaged file fails its SHA-256 check and is downloaded again. Check the network and that there is room for the model (about 1.5 GB for LFM3-Audio-2B, less for the others). Keep the app open while it downloads on the Mac.

troubleshooting.symptom: Apple Speech says it "can’t transcribe this language on this device"
troubleshooting.fix: Apple Speech has no model for the chosen language on this device, or the system hasn't downloaded it yet. Pick another language under Settings › Voice Input › Language (Automatic is the device's language), tap Download the Language when it's offered, or choose a downloaded model under Model.

troubleshooting.symptom: Voice input keeps writing a name or word wrong
troubleshooting.fix: Add it under Settings › Voice Input › Dictionary. With Heard As left empty the model is only told to expect the word; put what voice input writes instead under Heard As and every transcript gets the word in its place.

troubleshooting.symptom: "Microphone access is off" when tapping the mic
troubleshooting.fix: Yorozu was denied the microphone. Allow it in Settings › Privacy & Security › Microphone (iPhone and iPad) or System Settings › Privacy & Security › Microphone (Mac); the alert's Open Settings button goes there.

troubleshooting.symptom: Voice input says "No speech was recognized.", "No microphone is available." or "Not enough memory to transcribe."
troubleshooting.fix: No speech: speak closer to the microphone, or set Settings › Voice Input › Language to the language you speak; with LFM3-Audio-2B, unclear audio it can only repeat or answer with the dictionary also ends here, so try Whisper Large v3 Turbo. No microphone: connect or select an input device (Mac). Not enough memory: close other apps and tap Retry; the clip is kept until a transcript is delivered.

troubleshooting.symptom: Adding a Mac from an iPhone or iPad fails with "Couldn’t reach the relay. Check the connection and scan again."
troubleshooting.fix: The Mac's pairing code goes through the public relay's one-time mailbox, even with a self-hosted relay. Check both devices' internet connection and scan the Mac's current code again; the code changes every 10 minutes.

troubleshooting.symptom: `plugins install` is refused with `Plugin config repair could not be inspected: yorozu …`
troubleshooting.fix: OpenClaw's state still holds a pending migration for an older plugin with the id `yorozu`. `openclaw doctor --fix` runs the pending repair, but it rewrites OpenClaw state and also acts on other plugins' pending migrations.

troubleshooting.symptom: `channels status` shows Yorozu `recovering` with `unable to get local issuer certificate`
troubleshooting.fix: Node cannot verify the relay's TLS certificate because its OpenSSL has no CA bundle. Restore that OpenSSL's CA bundle, then run `openclaw gateway restart`.

troubleshooting.symptom: `channels status` shows `recovering` with another error
troubleshooting.fix: The relay is unreachable. The plugin redials with backoff (up to 30 s) and registers again by itself.

troubleshooting.symptom: The channel stops with `yorozu host key file is malformed`
troubleshooting.fix: The host key file is damaged. Restore it from a backup. Deleting it makes a new room, and every device has to pair again.

troubleshooting.symptom: `Configured plugin load path is unavailable: …/plugins/openclaw-yorozu`
troubleshooting.fix: The linked directory is gone (for example, a removed worktree). Install again with `--link` from a checkout that exists.

troubleshooting.symptom: `OpenClaw does not know the command "yorozu"`
troubleshooting.fix: The plugin is not installed in this profile, or the Gateway has not been restarted since the install.

troubleshooting.symptom: `openclaw yorozu pair` or `devices` cannot connect, or `pair` fails with `the yorozu channel is not connected to its relay`
troubleshooting.fix: The Gateway is not running, or the channel is not connected. Check `openclaw channels status`. For a non-default port or a remote Gateway, pass `--port`, or `--url` with `--token`.

troubleshooting.symptom: The app shows "Couldn’t pair", or "Removed from the host" right after pairing
troubleshooting.fix: The relay refused the token (`unknown token` or `expired token`: already used, or older than 10 minutes), or the plugin no longer holds the pairing secret (used, expired, or the Gateway restarted). Run `openclaw yorozu pair` again.

troubleshooting.symptom: The app says "Update required"
troubleshooting.fix: The client and the plugin share no protocol version. Update the older side.

troubleshooting.symptom: "Edit in Chat" or session tools are refused by the agent
troubleshooting.fix: `yorozu:owner` is not in `commands.ownerAllowFrom` ([Owner-only tools](#owner-only-tools)).

ios.title: Set up Yorozu on iPhone or iPad

steps.title: Install the Yorozu plugin on the computer that runs OpenClaw
steps.text: Yorozu needs your own OpenClaw Gateway (2026.9.8 or later). Run these on that computer, from a checkout of the Yorozu repository that will stay in place.
steps.details:
```sh
openclaw plugins install --link plugins/openclaw-yorozu --force --accept-capabilities
openclaw gateway restart
openclaw channels status
```

- `--link` loads the plugin from this directory, and code changes load on the next Gateway restart. Link from a checkout that stays, not from a worktree that will be removed.
- `--force` accepts a source that is not on ClawHub. `--accept-capabilities` gives the capability consent that the install otherwise stops to ask for.
- No `channels.yorozu` entry is needed, because every key has a default ([Config](#2-config)).
- On first start the plugin makes its host keys. The Gateway log shows `yorozu started (agent <agent>, room <room id>)`, then `yorozu: registered at relay, room <room id>`, and `openclaw channels status` shows the Yorozu channel connected.
- The Mac app also carries a copy of the plugin at `Yorozu.app/Contents/Resources/openclaw-channel`. A Gateway linked there runs the plugin version of the installed app.

The `openclaw yorozu` commands reach the running plugin through Gateway methods, so the Gateway must be running with the channel connected. They accept the usual Gateway client options (`--url`, `--port`, `--token`, `--password`, `--timeout`).

To try the plugin without touching a Gateway in use, run it in an isolated OpenClaw profile ([plugin README](../plugins/openclaw-yorozu/README.md#trying-it-without-the-main-gateway)).

steps.title: Check the config (optional)
steps.text: Every key under channels.yorozu has a default, so no config is needed. Change `channels.yorozu.agent` to pick which agent answers. Use list_settings for every key.

steps.title: Install the app
steps.text: Install Yorozu from the App Store on the iPhone or iPad.

steps.title: Pair the device
steps.text: On the Gateway computer run `openclaw yorozu pair`, then in the app tap Scan QR Code and scan it. Check that the host key matches the fingerprint the command printed.
steps.details:
```sh
openclaw yorozu pair
```

The command prints a QR code, a `yorozu://pair?…` link, the host fingerprint and the expiry time. The code works for one device, within 10 minutes, and only until the next Gateway restart.

1. In the app, on "Pair with your host", do one of these:
   - On iPhone or iPad, tap Scan QR Code and scan the code.
   - On any device, paste the link (or the https link the QR encodes) with Paste, or type it into "Pairing link" and tap Pair.
2. The app asks "Pair with this host?" and shows the host key. Pair only if it matches the fingerprint the command printed.
3. Pairing is done when the conversation list appears and `openclaw yorozu devices` lists the device by its model name. The app then asks to allow notifications.

**From a paired device:** Settings › Add a Device… makes a fresh pairing code on the host and shows it as a QR code and a link.

**A new Mac from a paired iPhone or iPad:** the Mac's pairing screen shows a code, which changes every 10 minutes.

1. On the iPhone or iPad, open Settings › Add a Device › Scan a Mac's Code (or point the Camera at the code) and tap Add.
2. On the Mac, check that the host key matches and click Pair.

Pair each device separately; all of them see the same conversations. At most 16 devices can be paired: a 17th replaces the oldest.

### Try demo data without a host

On the pairing screen, enter `YOROZU-DEMO` in **Pairing link** and tap **Pair**, or scan a QR code containing that text. Surrounding whitespace is ignored, and the code is case-sensitive. Demo mode shows sample conversations and automations and gives scripted replies; no host is involved. Settings › **Exit Demo** leaves it, and the existing pairing is kept.

For development, launch with `--demo` to start in demo mode directly. On the Mac, use a dev build with its own bundle id ([release.md](release.md#compile-checks)):

```sh
open -n .build/xcode-mac/Build/Products/Debug/YorozuIOS.app --args --demo
```

On an iOS Simulator with the app installed, run `xcrun simctl launch <udid> to.yumi.yorozu.ios --demo`.

steps.title: Allow notifications
steps.text: The app asks right after pairing. Allowing it lets replies arrive as push notifications while the app is closed.

steps.title: Turn on voice input (optional)
steps.text: Settings › Voice Input downloads the on-device voice model from Apple (about 1.44 GB, on Wi-Fi unless you allow cellular). Needs iOS 26 or later and about 6 GB of RAM.

2. The app asks "Pair with this host?" and shows the host key. Pair only if it matches the fingerprint the command printed.
3. Pairing is done when the conversation list appears and `openclaw yorozu devices` lists the device by its model name. The app then asks to allow notifications.

**From a paired device:** Settings › Add a Device… makes a fresh pairing code on the host and shows it as a QR code and a link.

**A new Mac from a paired iPhone or iPad:** the Mac's pairing screen shows a code, which changes every 10 minutes.

1. On the iPhone or iPad, open Settings › Add a Device › Scan a Mac's Code (or point the Camera at the code) and tap Add.
2. On the Mac, check that the host key matches and click Pair.

Pair each device separately; all of them see the same conversations. At most 16 devices can be paired: a 17th replaces the oldest.

### Try demo data without a host

On the pairing screen, enter `YOROZU-DEMO` in **Pairing link** and tap **Pair**, or scan a QR code containing that text. Surrounding whitespace is ignored, and the code is case-sensitive. Demo mode shows sample conversations and automations and gives scripted replies; no host is involved. Settings › **Exit Demo** leaves it, and the existing pairing is kept.

For development, launch with `--demo` to start in demo mode directly. On the Mac, use a dev build with its own bundle id ([release.md](release.md#compile-checks)):

```sh
open -n .build/xcode-mac/Build/Products/Debug/YorozuIOS.app --args --demo
```

On an iOS Simulator with the app installed, run `xcrun simctl launch <udid> to.yumi.yorozu.ios --demo`.

steps.title: Allow notifications
steps.text: The app asks right after pairing. The Mac gets no push; while Yorozu runs, replies in other conversations post local notifications.

steps.title: Turn on voice input (optional)
steps.text: Settings › Voice Input downloads the on-device voice model from Hugging Face (about 1.44 GB, checked by SHA-256). macOS asks for the microphone the first time you record.
